# I Don't Have a Will

> Free, plain-English guide to what makes a will valid in each U.S. state — witness rules, notarization, handwritten (holographic) wills, spousal protection, and probate — with primary-source statutory citations.

I Don't Have a Will helps people who have no estate plan understand what happens if they die intestate, exactly what their state requires for a valid will, and how to take a first step. Every state page cites the controlling statute (verified against the state's primary legislative source), leads with a direct answer to the question searchers ask, and is not legal advice.

## State will-requirement guides (with editorial "deep dives")
These states have in-depth, primary-source-cited analysis of their specific will law:
- [California](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/california) — holographic wills valid; notarization neither required nor sufficient; community-property spousal protection (no elective share)
- [New York](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/new-york) — strict execution; must "publish" the will; elective share (greater of $50,000 or 1/3); no holographic wills
- [Texas](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/texas) — holographic wills valid; community property; no notarization required; no harmless-error rule
- [Florida](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/florida) — no holographic wills; sign at the end; electronic wills legal since 2020; homestead devise restriction
- [Pennsylvania](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/pennsylvania) — witnesses prove the will at probate, not at signing; sign at the end; state inheritance tax by relationship
- [Illinois](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/illinois) — no holographic wills; spousal renunciation 1/3–1/2; electronic wills + remote witnessing
- [Ohio](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/ohio) — no holographic wills; no self-proving affidavit; spousal election against the will
- [Georgia](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/georgia) — no elective share (spouse can be disinherited, protected only by 12-month Year's Support); age 14 to make a will; no holographic wills
- [North Carolina](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/north-carolina) — holographic wills valid; sliding-scale elective share (15%–50% by marriage length); Clerk of Superior Court probate
- [Michigan](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements/michigan) — holographic wills valid if dated; harmless-error rescue; fill-in-the-blank statutory will form

## Key pages
- [Will Requirements by State](https://idonthaveawill.com/will-requirements) — all 50 states
- [Estate Planning Overview](https://idonthaveawill.com/estate-planning)

## State coverage
All 50 states are covered under `/will-requirements/[state]`, each with witness rules, notarization requirements, holographic-will treatment, spousal protection, and intestate-succession basics. The states listed above additionally carry a cited editorial deep dive.

## Important
This site is informational only. It is NOT legal advice. Statutory citations reflect the law as of 2026; laws change. Users with complex estates should consult a licensed attorney in their state.
